Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Amit Kumar Asthana
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rahul Chaturvedi,J.
Heard Shri Amit Kumar Asthana, learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

By means of the present application the applicant is invoking the plenary powers of this Court u/s 482 Cr.P.C. seeking the prayer "to quash the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No.2036 of 2020 (State vs. Udairaj), arising out of Case Crime No.176 of 2018, u/s 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C.,
Police Station-Devgaon, District-Azamgarh, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.10, Azamgarh."
Submission raised by learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is only a marginal witness to the alleged forged sale-deed between Surendra Tiwari s/o Sabhajit and the purchaser is Furkan and the present F.I.R. was registered against as many as 9 named accused persons, but the charge sheet was submitted by the police only against the applicant, who is a practicing advocate Udai Raj Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180288159/

sentences.text: and happens to be a marginal witness of the alleged sale-deed.

Learned counsel for the applicant has contended that neither the applicant is a beneficiary nor the property in question belongs to him and he has been nailed down in this case only because of being the marginal witness.

It is also contended by learned counsel that all the accused persons who are either seller or purchaser of the deed have come to terms outside the court and accordingly civil proceedings having O.S.
Nos.2195/2018, 2196/2018 and 2197/2018 have been filed, which were decreed in favour of the parties on the basis of compromise vide order dated 8.12.2018.
All the aforesaid civil suits have been decided in the light of compromise arrived at between the parties.

As mentioned above, the applicant is only a marginal witness of the alleged sale-deed and has earned nothing from these deals, as such, the applicant is directed to appear before the trial court within 15 days from today and move an application u/s 88 Cr.P.C.
The trial court, after ensuring the presence of the applicant, shall release him with or without sureties by a suitable order within a week thereafter.

After being released, the applicant is at liberty to move a discharge application before the trial court raising all points canvassed before this Court, which would be heard and decided by the concerned court within a period of eight weeks from its institution by a well reasoned order.
Till the disposal of said discharge application moved on behalf of applicant, he shall not be arrested in aforesaid case.

It is made clear that in the event the 'Discharge Application' is decided against the applicant, then the applicant would have no other option but to surrender before the court concerned and apply for regular bail.
This application stands disposed off with above observations.

Order Date :- 23.3.2023 M. Kumar  Udai Raj Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180288159/
